content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper addresses minimization of complexity of representations spaces for HSBRL. To this end, this paper proposes a sparse learning scheme for hyperbolic space using a our novel sparse regularization term and optimization algorithm. Experimental analyses show that the proposed scheme can obtain sparse representations with smaller information loss than Riemannian Gradient Descent.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper addresses an important problem of learning on hyperbolic spaces with sparse models. Therefore, the paper spends pretty much effort to construct a new method for learning on hyperbolic spaces.

However, there are various major and minor problems with the paper while addressing this problem. Briefly, there are unclear definitions and proposed methods are not employed correctly following common definitions and structures of manifolds. In addition, experimental analyses should be improved.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
First, Section 2, 3 and 4 can be simplified by moving minor results and statements to the supp. mat., and only keeping the major methods in the main text. 

Second, several parts of the proposed methods and experimental details are unclear. 

For instance, graph_p(L) is defined as a Riemannian gradient. Then, why do you map on a manifold again using exp to a manifold? Indeed, if both points moved by the Riemannian gradient and the new manifold are the same, then exp will not have an effect. If they are on different manifolds, then you may need to use other projections.

In addition, it is not clear how Riemannian Gradient Descent (RGD) is implemented in the analyses. First, Algorithm 1 is an RGD method. Then, how does Algorithm 1 differ from RGD on hyperbolic manifolds? Second, how did you implement variations of RGDs (i.e. 1-norm RGD, linear 1 norm  RGD and no-regularization RGD) with different sparsity structures in Fig. 1? These results show that the proposed methods and RGDs perform similarly. Therefore, the novelty and contribution of the proposed methods are not clear.

Moreover, the proposed methods should be explored with additional datasets and tasks to show novelty and benefits of the proposed methods more clearly.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a framework for learning sparse representations on a general Riemannian manfold, with particular interest in Hyperbolic space. The sparse concept is well-defined, together with a modified iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm on the manifold. Simple experiments were conducted to evaluate and analyze the proposed algorithm.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

-- The sparse representation is novel and well-defined in theory for general Riemannian manifolds. 

-- The text is clear and logic is easy to follow and understand. 

-- Well-cited related work. 

Weakness:

-- The only weakness is in the experiment, as most of the paper is theory and concepts. In figure 1, the y-axis balanced accuracy is high for nearly all, and the improvement looks minor to me using hyperbolic 1 norm + HISTA, can you provide a relative improvement value for it against baselines? 

-- Somehow the improvement from hyperbolic 1 norm + HISTA does not meet my expectation, can the authors explain? is it because the dataset too small and dimension low? 

Question:

-- In corollary 1 the hyperbolic STO, where is the max function compared to 0, just as that in the STO function? 

-- page 18, the algorithm, the $q^{t-1}$ term is computed but never used in the algorithm, why? 

Typo:

-- page 6, second paragraph, line 7, "and weak regularization could" --> "and weak regularization around the root could" 

-- page 8, last paragraph before Section 5, $\epsilon=10^3$ --> $\epsilon=10^{-3}$

-- page 15 in the appendix, remove the extra period.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The quality of the paper is good, clear text and logic, well-defined theory, novel work.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall I like this paper as it is well-motivated in theory, despite of the minor improvements in experiments, an experiment on large dataset to show the superiority of the algorithm will make the paper stronger.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper considers a generalization of sparse Euclidean embeddings to hyperbolic embeddings. The approach can be summarized as follows: The tangent space of every $D$-dimensional Riemannian manifold admits an orthonormal basis $e_1, \dots, e_D$. In the Euclidean case, the $\ell_0$-norm of $x$ is the number of non-zero elements of $x$. By taking into account the isomorphism between $\mathbb{R}^D$ and its tangent space at the origin $0$ $T_{0} \mathbb{R}^D$ (i.e. $\mathbb{R}^D \approx T_{0} \mathbb{R}^D$ ), each tangent vector can be identified by a point. The $\ell_0$-norm of $x$ then becomes equivalent to the number of elements of $x$ such that the (Euclidean) distance between $x^i$ and $0$ is $0$. Since the $\ell_0$-norm is NP-hard to optimize, it is often relaxed by the $\ell_1$-norm which is its convex surrogate. 

The paper proposes an extension of the $\ell_0$ and $\ell_1$-norms to some hyperbolic embeddings.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weakness 1: The idea is interesting but limited to some Riemannian geometries such as the Klein and Poincare geometries. First, as stated in Definition 4, it assumes that there is a (global) diffeomorphism between $T_0 \mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}$, which is not the case for many Riemannian manifolds such as the sphere. The diffeomorphism of the exponential map is generally local on a neighborhood, which is $T_0 \mathcal{M}$ for the Euclidean, Klein and Poincare geometries.

Weakness 2: The paper only considers sparse embeddings. However, sparsity is usually promoted on the parameters of some model in machine learning. For instance for Support Vector Machines (SVMs), a model parameterized by some vector $w \in \mathbb{R}^D$ is learned and a regularization involving its $\ell_1$-norm $\| \| w \| \|_1$ is added. This submission does not consider such learning scheme. 
Moreover, most hyperbolic neural networks have their learnable parameters lying in the tangent space of some reference point. Since a tangent space of a Riemannian manifold is a local Euclidean approximation of the manifold. It would be straightforward to extend sparse neural networks in such tangent spaces, and the proposed approach becomes unnecessary. 

Weakness 3: The motivation of using such an approach in real-world applications is not clear. As discussed above, most real-world applications would learn neural networks whose parameters lie in some tangent space, and extensions of Euclidean sparse models become straightforward. The experimental section does not motivate how the proposed approach would be useful in practice.

Typo: there is a typo in the second line of Example 3, it should be $\Pi_d^{\mathcal{M}} = \{ p \in \mathbb{R}^D | p^{\top} e_d = 0 \}$, not $\Pi_d^{\mathcal{M}} = \{p \in \mathbb{R}^D | p^{\top} e_D = 0\}$
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The approach and explanation is clear and straightforward but limited to some types of Riemannian geometries. It also does not seem useful in practice.

content.title: Sparse Hyperbolic Representation Learning
content.TL;DR: The paper proposes sparse regularization for hyperbolic-space-based machine learning.
content.abstract: Reducing the space complexity of representations while minimizing the loss of information makes data science procedures computationally efficient. For the entities with the tree structure, hyperbolic-space-based representation learning (HSBRL) has successfully reduced the space complexity of representations by using low-dimensional space. Nevertheless, it has not minimized the space complexity of each representation since it has used the same dimension for all representations and has not selected the best dimension for each representation. Hence, this paper aims to minimize representations' space complexity for HSBRL. For minimizing each representation's space complexity, sparse learning has been effective in the context of linear-space-based machine learning; however, no sparse learning has been proposed for HSBRL.  It is non-trivial to propose sparse learning for HSBRL because (i) sparse learning methods designed for linear space cause non-uniform sparseness in hyperbolic space, and (ii) existing Riemannian gradient descent methods fail to obtain sparse representations owing to an oscillation problem. This paper, for the first time, establishes a sparse learning scheme for hyperbolic space, overcoming the above issues with our novel sparse regularization term and optimization algorithm. Our regularization term achieves uniform sparseness since it is defined based on geometric distance from subspaces inducing sparsity. Our optimization algorithm successfully obtains sparse representations, avoiding the oscillation problem by realizing the shrinkage-thresholding idea in a general Riemannian manifold. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our scheme can obtain sparse representations with smaller information loss than traditional methods, successfully avoiding the oscillation problem.
